routes.title: Model routes
routes.lede: Every login and API key that serves each model, in priority order, with the cooldowns Provimux recorded on them.
routes.load_failed: Could not load the model routes
routes.note: Among the routes that can serve a new request, a higher priority is tried first, and routes that share a priority are chosen between by the routing strategy; a session already on a route may stay there. A recorded cooldown is the timer Provimux wrote after a refused request, with its reason. It is not an availability verdict: a route without one can still fail (an expired login, for one), and Auth Files shows each login's state.

devin.title: Devin: quota pause per model
devin.eyebrow: When a Devin login runs out of its daily or weekly quota
devin.on_text: On: only the model Devin refused is paused until the quota resets; Devin keeps serving the models it does not meter (swe-2, swe-2-flash).
devin.off_text: Off: the whole login pauses until the quota resets, including the models Devin keeps serving without a quota (swe-2, swe-2-flash). Turn it on to pause only the refused model.
devin.limit_note: Known limit: Provimux may not learn when the quota resets, so it tries a paused model again now and then, waiting longer each time (from 1 second up to 30 minutes; each try is one quick refused request).
devin.saved_on: Devin pauses only the refused model now
devin.saved_off: Devin pauses the whole login again
devin.none_cooling: No Devin model is cooling down ({{count}} models).
devin.absent_no_login: No Devin login. The switch applies when you add one.

live.title: Live model lists
live.lede: Each Claude, Codex and Meta login can register the models its own account lists, not only the shared catalog: retired models disappear and new ones appear the day the provider lists them.
live.load_failed: Could not load the live lists
live.on_text: On: each login asks its provider for its model list at startup, every 3 hours and when you refresh. Until a list arrives, or while fetches fail, the catalog or the last good list is used, so an outage never empties a login. A login file replaced by another account never keeps the old list.
live.off_text: Off: every login uses the built-in catalog. Turn it on to have each Claude, Codex and Meta login register what its own account lists. It applies at once.
live.refresh_hint: Asks the server to refresh the model catalogs and each login's list in the background. Each row below shows its login's state as of the latest status read.

live.refresh_catalog_failed: The server could not refresh the built-in model list ({{message}}). Each login's list on its routes updates on the next read.
live.refresh_unconfirmed: Could not confirm the request: the server may still be refreshing. Each login's list on its routes updates on the next read.
live.saved_off: Live lists are off; every login uses the catalog

headline.title: Worth of prompt caching
headline.text: Valued at API list prices, net of what writing the cache cost: every input token at the input price, minus what the cached mix cost. Only the part on API keys is money saved.
headline.apikey_text: money that would have been paid
headline.oauth_text: saves quota, not dollars; value at list price
headline.negative: Caching cost more than it was worth in this period: the cache was written and not read enough to pay for the writes.
headline.negative_partial: For the {{priced}} of {{requests}} requests with a price, caching cost more than it was worth: their cache was written and not read enough to pay for the writes. This says nothing about the period as a whole: the requests without a price can change the sign.
headline.unvalued: No amount: nothing in this period has a price, so nothing can be valued.
headline.partial: Only the {{priced}} of {{requests}} requests with a price are in this amount. It is not a lower bound: a request without a price can be worth less than nothing, because writing the cache costs more than plain input.
headline.text_base: Valued at base API list prices, net of what writing the cache cost: every input token at the input price, minus what the cached mix cost. Only the part on API keys is money saved.

models.order_note: Order: among the routes that can take a new request, Provimux tries the highest priority first; routes with the same priority share the requests, and a conversation already on a route may stay there. A priority belongs to a login or an API key, so it applies to every model it serves: an API key's is set here or on Accounts, a login's on Accounts. A cooldown is the timer Provimux recorded after a refused request, with its reason; a route without one can still fail.

restarts.title: Restarts
restarts.lede: What a stop, a restart or an upgrade does to the answers in flight and to the conversations under way, as the gateway reports it. Saving here restarts nothing: the gateway takes each change up while it runs.
restarts.config_failed: Could not read the configuration file, so nothing can be changed here: {{message}}
restarts.step_stop_text: While the gateway stops, it accepts no new requests; a tool that tries again once it is back can reach it.
restarts.step_answers_wait_one: HTTP answers in flight get up to {{count}} second to finish; what is still running then is cut.
restarts.step_answers_wait_other: HTTP answers in flight get up to {{count}} seconds to finish; what is still running then is cut.
restarts.step_answers_cut: HTTP answers in flight are cut: a tool may get a partial answer or an error.
restarts.step_answers_unreported: This gateway does not report how long it waits.
restarts.step_answers_unread: The page could not read how long the gateway waits.
restarts.step_back_kept: Conversations that send their own session id go back to the account they were on, if the gateway still recognises it and the binding has not expired, so the provider can read their prompt cache again, if it still holds it.
restarts.step_back_in_use: Another Provimux on the same store holds the snapshot's lock: this one cannot save now, and at its start it restores, from a snapshot it can authenticate, what is still valid.
restarts.step_back_no_affinity: Session affinity, which keeps a conversation's requests on one account, is off: each request is routed on its own, before and after the restart.
restarts.step_back_not_kept: Accounts are not kept: routing picks an account for each conversation again, possibly another one, where the provider may have to build the prompt cache again.
restarts.step_back_unreported: The page cannot tell: this gateway does not report what it keeps across a restart.
restarts.step_back_unread: The page cannot tell: it could not read what the gateway keeps.
restarts.absent_not_provimux: This gateway ({{version}}) is not Provimux and does not have this setting.
restarts.absent_unknown: This gateway does not report this setting, so the console does not show or change it.
restarts.absent_since: The console shows and changes it from Provimux {{since}}.
restarts.absent_since_newer: The console shows and changes it with a newer Provimux.
restarts.drain_switch_label: Let answers in flight finish when the gateway stops
restarts.drain_on_text: When the gateway stops, it waits this long at most for the HTTP answers in flight; the wait ends as soon as they are done. It does not wait for answers over a Responses WebSocket connection or through the AI Studio relay.
restarts.drain_off_text: When the gateway stops, it does not wait: HTTP answers in flight are cut, and a tool may get a partial answer or an error.
restarts.drain_default_note: Not set in the configuration file: the gateway's default applies.
restarts.drain_default_follows: Here the default follows the gateway's general stop timeout (server.shutdown-timeout: {{seconds}}).
restarts.drain_stop_limit_one: The gateway ends a stop after at most {{limit}} seconds, so it waits {{count}} second at most.
restarts.drain_stop_limit_other: The gateway ends a stop after at most {{limit}} seconds, so it waits {{count}} seconds at most.
restarts.drain_refused: The configuration file says {{written}}, which the gateway refuses. While the file holds it, the gateway keeps its last valid wait, shown above, and a restart with this file fails to start. Save a value here to replace it.
restarts.drain_clamped: The configuration file says {{written}}; the gateway uses {{used}}, the nearest value it takes ({{min}} to {{max}}).
restarts.drain_not_loaded_one: The configuration file says {{written}}, but the running gateway still waits up to {{count}} second: it has not loaded the file yet.
restarts.drain_not_loaded_other: The configuration file says {{written}}, but the running gateway still waits up to {{count}} seconds: it has not loaded the file yet.
restarts.drain_not_loaded_default_one: The configuration file sets no value, but the running gateway still waits up to {{count}} second: it has not loaded the file yet.
restarts.drain_not_loaded_default_other: The configuration file sets no value, but the running gateway still waits up to {{count}} seconds: it has not loaded the file yet.
restarts.drain_file_error: The gateway could not read its configuration file, so the page cannot tell what the file sets: {{message}}
restarts.drain_failed: Could not read the gateway's wait: {{message}}
restarts.drain_absent_in_file: This Provimux ({{version}}) has this setting but does not report it, so the console cannot show or change it: set server.restart-drain-seconds in its configuration file.
restarts.drain_absent_older: This Provimux ({{version}}) does not have this setting.
restarts.cost_wait_one: A stop can take up to {{count}} second longer while answers finish.
restarts.cost_wait_other: A stop can take up to {{count}} seconds longer while answers finish.
restarts.cost_turn_off: Turned off, the gateway stops without waiting, and answers in flight are cut.
restarts.cost_turn_on_one: Turned on, the gateway's default applies: it waits up to {{count}} second for answers in flight when it stops.
restarts.cost_turn_on_other: Turned on, the gateway's default applies: it waits up to {{count}} seconds for answers in flight when it stops.
restarts.use_default_hint: Clears the value in the configuration file, so the gateway's default applies
restarts.service_note: The program that stops the gateway has to allow this long. Homebrew's service allows 40 seconds (Homebrew 6.0.13 or newer). Docker allows 10 seconds unless given more: docker stop -t 40, or stop_grace_period: 40s in Compose.
restarts.drain_saved_wait_one: Saved. The gateway now waits up to {{count}} second for answers in flight when it stops.
restarts.drain_saved_wait_other: Saved. The gateway now waits up to {{count}} seconds for answers in flight when it stops.
restarts.drain_saved_none: Saved. The gateway now stops without waiting for answers in flight.
restarts.drain_saved_not_shown_wait_one: Saved in the configuration file, but the gateway still reports a wait of up to {{count}} second. Reload in a moment.
restarts.drain_saved_not_shown_wait_other: Saved in the configuration file, but the gateway still reports a wait of up to {{count}} seconds. Reload in a moment.
restarts.drain_saved_not_shown_none: Saved in the configuration file, but the gateway still reports no wait. Reload in a moment.
restarts.drain_unconfirmed_wait_one: The gateway did not confirm the save. It now reports a wait of up to {{count}} second.
restarts.drain_unconfirmed_wait_other: The gateway did not confirm the save. It now reports a wait of up to {{count}} seconds.
restarts.drain_unconfirmed_none: The gateway did not confirm the save. It now reports no wait.
restarts.persist_switch_label: Keep conversations on their account across a restart
restarts.persist_on_text: When it stops and every 5 minutes, the gateway saves, encrypted, which account each conversation is on, for the conversations and accounts it can recognise; the counts below say how many were left out. At the next start, conversations that send their own session id go back to the account they were on, if the gateway still recognises it and the binding has not expired, so the provider can read their prompt cache again, if it still holds it.
restarts.persist_limits: Not restored: a conversation without its own session id on a gateway with client keys, and accounts the gateway cannot recognise after a restart, such as a Kimi login, an AI Studio connection or a login a plugin made.
restarts.persist_off_text: Off in the configuration file: the gateway saves no new snapshot and removes its own files where it can. After a restart, routing picks an account for each conversation again.
restarts.persist_off_also: Turned on, it would still not be in effect: {{reason}}
restarts.reason_session_affinity_off: Session affinity, which keeps a conversation's requests on one account, is off, so there is nothing to keep. Turn it on in Routing; the gateway then says whether anything else stops it.
restarts.reason_home_mode: The gateway runs in Home mode, where conversations' accounts are not kept across a restart.
restarts.reason_kv_store_off: The gateway's local storage is turned off (server.kv-store.disabled), so it cannot save conversations' accounts.
restarts.reason_foreign_file: A file the gateway does not recognise as its own is where the snapshot goes. The gateway leaves it untouched and saves nothing until it is moved away or removed.
restarts.reason_key_not_private: The key file belongs to another user, or its permissions are wider than owner read and write and the gateway could not narrow them, so the gateway does not use it.
restarts.reason_directory_not_writable: The gateway cannot write in its local storage folder.
restarts.reason_path_unusable: The gateway cannot use its snapshot file's path.
restarts.reason_in_use: Another Provimux on the same store holds the snapshot's lock, so this one cannot save now. At its start it can still restore, from a snapshot it can authenticate, what is still valid, and it tries to save again once the lock is released.
restarts.not_written_yet: None saved in this run yet: the gateway tries to save when it stops and every 5 minutes.
restarts.left_out_one: {{count}} left out: the gateway could not verify that its account stayed the same.
restarts.left_out_other: {{count}} left out: the gateway could not verify that their accounts stayed the same.
restarts.left_out_no_identity_one: {{count}} left out: its account has no identity the gateway can recognise after a restart.
restarts.left_out_no_identity_other: {{count}} left out: their accounts have no identity the gateway can recognise after a restart.
restarts.restored_one: {{count}} saved conversation was put back on its account.
restarts.restored_other: {{count}} saved conversations were put back on their account.
restarts.restored_unknown_one: {{count}} was on an account the gateway could not match to a current one.
restarts.restored_unknown_other: {{count}} were on accounts the gateway could not match to current ones.
restarts.restored_other_build_one: {{count}} could not be restored: this version names or keeps that conversation differently.
restarts.restored_other_build_other: {{count}} could not be restored: this version names or keeps those conversations differently.
restarts.start_no_snapshot: No saved snapshot was found. That is expected before the first successful save: after an upgrade from a version without it, or after turning it on.
restarts.start_not_in_effect: Nothing was restored: it was not in effect at that start.
restarts.start_failed: The snapshot could not be restored: {{message}}
restarts.last_error_not_removed: The gateway could not remove its own files from an earlier run: {{message}}
restarts.key_note: The key file's permissions were wider than owner read and write; the gateway narrowed them.
restarts.files_text: The snapshot can be read only with the key.
restarts.turn_off_cost: Turned off, the gateway saves no new snapshot and removes its own files where it can; after a restart, routing picks an account for each conversation again.
restarts.turn_on_cost: Turned on (the default), the gateway saves, whenever it is in effect, which account each conversation is on, for the conversations and accounts it can recognise.
restarts.persist_saved_in_effect: Saved. The gateway reports it in effect.
restarts.persist_saved_not_in_effect: Saved. The gateway reports it not in effect, for the reason above.
restarts.persist_saved_off: Saved. The gateway reports it off.
restarts.persist_saved_not_shown: Saved in the configuration file, but the gateway does not report the new setting yet. Reload in a moment.
restarts.persist_unconfirmed_in_effect: The gateway did not confirm the save. It now reports it on and in effect.
restarts.persist_unconfirmed_not_in_effect: The gateway did not confirm the save. It now reports it on, but not in effect.
restarts.persist_unconfirmed_off: The gateway did not confirm the save. It now reports it off.
restarts.persist_failed: Could not read what the gateway keeps: {{message}}
restarts.applying: Saved. Waiting for the gateway to report it…
restarts.saved_unread: Saved in the configuration file. The page could not read the gateway again to see whether it took it up.
restarts.unconfirmed_unread: The gateway did not confirm the save, and the page could not read it again. Reload to see what it reports.
restarts.stale_absent: Nothing was sent: the gateway no longer reports this setting; it may have been replaced by another version. The page shows what it reports now.
restarts.stale_changed: Nothing was sent: the gateway's setting changed since this page showed it. The page shows it as it is now.
restarts.stale_unreadable: Nothing was sent: the page could not check the gateway's setting first.
restarts.err_changed_reread: The configuration file changed since this page read it, so nothing was written. The page shows it as it is now.
restarts.err_changed_unread: The configuration file changed since this page read it, so nothing was written. The page could not read it again.
restarts.err_no_tag: Couldn't check that the configuration file is the one this page read, so nothing was changed.
